baselineCaptures: source/round-01/baseline (backups/reef.py rendered with the same Blender)

notes: Ground rings: away from non-exposed corners, every new z=0 vertex lies on the original outline polyline and every original z=0 vertex on the new one (distances in cells). Non-exposed (groove, seam and square-footprint) corners are tightened from radius .05 to .015: tightCornerOutsideBox = 0 shows they never pass the slab box, i.e. the collision footprint. Exposed .35 corners are identical.
cornerChipBite: largest top bite w and inward corner move d of a corner chip (limit .03); nickBite: deepest groove-edge nick. Ground rings are never chipped.
topHeightDelta is the removed per-vertex top jitter (+/-.008 in the original); the generator sequence, tilt and per-slab heights are unchanged.
Groove core: hidden block inside the footprint (inset .03 from open faces, flush to faces against solid), below every slab top; the image footprint check confirms it adds no outline pixels.

Alpha footprint vs baseline: masks alpha>0.5 at native 768x2048, compared as outer silhouettes (morphological closing, 12 px radius) because the hidden core intentionally fills groove gaps (grooveFillPx). Shifts in native px (4 px = 1 logical px). Pixels opaque beyond the baseline (+2 px) and bottom-row shifts occur only on faces against solid: the core runs flush to those cell edges and square at non-exposed corners (the collision shape), closing the seabed notches the 0.05 slab corner rounding left at cell junctions; it never passes the footprint (geometry.pieces.*.coreInsideFootprint) or the slab tops. sideExtentShift excludes the 8 tangent rows at the top and bottom of the silhouette.
Repeat renders of an unchanged piece are pixel-identical (file bytes differ only in PNG metadata), so tolerance is 0 for renderer noise.

registration.lightChangesFromSource: fill colour (.90,.96,1) -> (.97,.96,.95), equal on all eight; positions, energies, sizes and overhead unchanged; round 03 turns cast shadows off on every light alike (in-piece shadows cannot match across cell seams)
